diffs.diff: TDS (ppm): datasheet reading gives 434.78 per count, the part's model has 1
diffs.evidence: 434.78 is just 1000 ppm / 2.3 V (range divided by output span), a linear mapping the datasheet never gives. The SEN0244 datasheet specifies 'Output Voltage: 0 ~ 2.3V', 'TDS Measurement Range: 0 ~ 1000ppm' and converts with a cubic: 'tdsValue=(133.42*V*V*V - 255.86*V*V + 857.39*V)*0.5; //convert voltage value to tds value' (DFRobot GravityTDS.cpp: ecValue=(133.42*V^3 - 255.86*V^2 + 857.39*V)*kValue; ecValue25=ecValue/(1.0+0.02*(T-25)); tdsValue=ecValue25*TdsFactor). The model's sim maps the A pin voltage 1:1 (0-2.3 V -> 0-2.3 V, scale 1 V/V) and the driver applies exactly this nonlinear DFRobot formula (e.g. 1.45 V -> 556 ppm; a linear 434.78 ppm/V would give 630 ppm and 2.3 V would be 1000 ppm instead of the formula's 1121 ppm). The model is right; the second reading compared a ppm-per-volt linearization against the model's volt-to-volt sim scale.
